# AI-Assisted SDLC Playbook — full agent context

Source of truth for humans: https://smg99.github.io/engineering-ai-playbook/
Machine signposts: /llm.txt · /llms.txt · this file
Repository: https://github.com/smg99/engineering-ai-playbook
Former name: Engineering AI Playbook

## Definition

The AI-Assisted SDLC Playbook is a free, public, tool-agnostic method for engineering teams to use approved AI tools across a full software development lifecycle. It provides nine stages with copyable prompts, inputs/outputs, and exit gates. It emphasizes human approval, readiness-only story validation before tickets, optional second-AI critique of review markdown, and verification with real tests and diffs. The website never creates tickets, runs code, or sends data to an AI provider.

## Not this

- Not a vendor product or model recommendation
- Not automatic Jira/Linear ticket creation
- Not a substitute for client security policy or approved tool lists
- Not permission to paste proprietary code or PHI into public chat

## Recommended workflow for vague requirements

1. Open SDLC home on the site.
2. Copy the **generate review-markdown** prompt into an approved AI tool; paste the requirement.
3. Save the private markdown (clarify → epic → design → stories → readiness-only).
4. Copy the **second-AI critique** prompt into a different approved model or fresh session; adapt useful feedback with the owner.
5. Create tickets only for the approved MVP set.
6. Use Develop one story → Verify → QA → Release for implementation.

## Stage prompt location

Exact stage prompt text lives in the live site UI and in assets/flow-data.js in the repository. Prefer copying from the live site so teams always get the published wording.

## Stage list (contract)

Clarify requirements → Define the epic → Design the approach → Draft stories → Review & create stories → Develop one story → Verify & review → QA validation → Release & monitor.

## Coverage policy (default wording)

Meet the project’s agreed coverage gate for new or changed application code (prefer 100% line, branch, function and statement when tooling supports it). State the actual gate if it differs. Report the existing repository baseline separately. Document measurement limitations and approved exclusions; do not silently weaken the target, exclude code to inflate coverage or claim coverage without execution.

## Security boundary

Public site and repo: generic guidance and synthetic examples only. Real tickets, code, credentials, and client operational data stay in approved private systems.

## Docs map

- docs/WORKFLOW.md — vague requirement to verified release
- docs/REVIEW-MD.md — generate + critique prompts for MD-first planning
- docs/TOOLS.md — approved tool / agent / MCP guidance
- docs/SECURITY.md — client separation
- docs/QUOTA-AND-HANDOFF.md — pause/resume and provider switching
- docs/CONTRIBUTING.md — how to extend stages and sync guides
